title: Crispy Chicken Nuggets with Spicy Cane's-Style Sauce
summary: Ground chicken breast is seasoned, shaped into nuggets, and frozen, then dipped in a light batter and fried at 350°F until golden and crisp. Serve them hot with a spicy mayonnaise sauce flavored with sriracha and Worcestershire.

items.original_text: ½ tsp paprika or chili powder
items.name: paprika or chili powder

items.original_text: Neutral oil, about 1½ inches deep in the pot
items.name: neutral oil
items.notes: about 1 1/2 inches deep in the pot

items.name: sriracha
items.notes: to 2 tbsp; start with 1 tbsp and add more to taste

items.original_text: ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper
items.name: black pepper

items: Mix the ground chicken breast, egg, cornstarch, and seasonings until smooth and sticky. Lightly oil your hands and shape into small nuggets about 1/2 inch thick. Place them on a parchment-lined tray and freeze for a few hours, until frozen.

Whisk together the flour, cornstarch, and seasonings for the wet batter. Start with 1/2 cup cold water and add more a little at a time until the batter coats the nuggets and the excess drips off easily.
Heat the oil to 350°F. Lightly coat each frozen nugget in plain flour, shake off the excess, then dip it into the wet batter. Let the extra batter drip off before frying.
Fry in small batches, turning occasionally, until golden and crispy. Start checking around 4–5 minutes and cook until the centers reach 165°F. Drain on a wire rack and let them rest for 1–2 minutes.
Mix the mayonnaise, sriracha, Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, and black pepper. Start with 1 tablespoon sriracha and add more to taste. Serve with the hot nuggets for dipping.

notes: The written recipe with quantities is the caption on platedbyyuri's Facebook reel.

The source does not give prep, cook, or total times. The method calls for freezing the shaped nuggets "for a few hours, until frozen," frying until the centers reach 165°F (start checking around 4–5 minutes), and resting 1–2 minutes after draining. Those times are in the steps; no overall time is listed.
Wet batter water is listed as 1/2–3/4 cup. The method says to start with 1/2 cup and add more a little at a time until the batter coats the nuggets and the excess drips off easily.
Sriracha is listed as 1–2 tablespoons. The method says to start with 1 tablespoon and add more to taste.
The wet batter calls for 1/2 teaspoon paprika or chili powder (either is fine).
Neutral oil is specified by depth (about 1 1/2 inches in the pot), not by volume.
The method says to lightly oil your hands when shaping the nuggets; that oil is not listed as a separate ingredient.
